summary:
The revised brief applies everything it was asked to. It applies my conditions 1-7 as I wrote them. It carries the test-engineer's conditions 1-5 and findings TE-CBB-1 to -12, applying eleven and deferring one (TE-CBB-11) in writing for a sound reason. It quotes his stop rules and size line word for word, and it changes nothing else. One stale sentence about the size needs a one-line fix. After that, the build can start from this brief.

**The previous version.** HEAD no longer holds it. The background autosave 09cca21 already committed the revised brief (sha256 cffbe065..., 662 lines). The previous version ba6bdeb0... (540 lines) is in commit c0387c7, so I diffed c0387c7 against 09cca21: 241 lines added, 119 removed, in 46 hunks. I read every hunk. Each one maps to an item in the reviser's map. My notes: .checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/advisor-c62h-bound-brief-rev.md.

**What I checked myself** (read only, no file written except my notes):
- **Stop rules and size line.** A script compared the brief's lines 603-607, with "> " removed, against paste lines 120-124: an exact match. Lines 609-611 joined match paste line 89 exactly. His words are cited at the right lines: history.md:2172-2175. The measured-scope line is paste :105, where my earlier :106 was off by one; the brief is right.
- **The planted-bug reading.** It is no narrower than his words. PM-0001-17's L1 P2 part carries exactly three checks: decoded_hash_mismatch_count and the two new ones. "Setup" belongs to the part "every S30", and "loses no group" to "L1 P0". So "the other new figure and decoded_hash_mismatch_count" is all of his "every other check".
- **The eight gap phrases** (brief :241-249) match the frozen row's gaps (texts v3:83), in the same order. One phrase writes out the row's "it" in full, which it must, to stay distinct from the next one.
- **The why-line placement** (TE-CBB-5) holds:
  - in the P0 verdict.json, -17's why list ends with whole-as-lost's "no run yet";
  - in verdict-bites.json, -17's why list holds no bite line.
  - Both files re-hash to e926b812... and b472784f....
- **The P0 precedent** (TE-CBB-3) holds. runs.txt :37 and :42 differ only in the run name, the client hashes (878352 against 878304), measured incomplete (0 against 48) and the wall time. The summary line's first field is the run name (scenario.rs:1621).
- **The test counts add up:** 538 + 7 + 6 + 1 = 552, and 616 + 9 + 6 + 1 = 632.
- **The l1 canonical bytes** are as the brief says: Down = 1 (lib.rs:235-240), flow code 0 = datagram (:262-268), kind 1 lost, 2 burst.
- **The reference sets exist:** fc411116c1f1/P2 and fd4612050cd6/P3.
- **Nothing else changed:**
  - Inputs unchanged: paste cfac7502, texts v3 3f21c9b7, freeze 9cb8be17, all as recorded at bedca79.
  - Untouched: section 2's insert algorithm and its four expected hashes; what either figure computes and its FIGURES text; 8.4's verdict lines; the order of steps.
  - The only additions are checks inside existing steps. No line is over 120 columns.
- **The size estimate:** about 650-875 lines, under the 1,050 stop.

**What I could not check.** I built and ran nothing from the lane. The scripts, the plants, the counts and the judged results are still to be shown by the build.
te_rulings:
TE condition 2 / TE-CBB-2: ACCEPT.
- Each gap case asserts its own phrase on both figures (:239-249, :271-278).
- Case 1 is pinned by the gap order (the reader returns its first gap), by its phrase, and by plant CB-P16.
- The pair that hid each other is split: case 2's note must hold the second phrase and not the first, with plant CB-P17.
- The wrong-length case uses tick.s.snap_link_lost_count, with plant CB-P18.
- One plant per pair, as the test-engineer offered.

TE condition 3 / TE-CBB-3: ACCEPT (:550-557). The comparison strips the run name, the new phrase and the wall time.
- whole-as-lost may differ from s1 in exactly two fields: client hashes minus 48 and measured incomplete plus 48.
- link-lost-overstated may differ in none.
- The new phrase's S, L, B, E1 and E2 equal s1's; N is 48 and 0.
- Any other differing field goes to the advisor.
The P0 precedent checked: runs.txt :37 against :42.

TE condition 4 / TE-CBB-4: ACCEPT (:334-339).
- Expected changes: +7 / +9, +6 / +6, +1 / +1, then 0 / 0; final 552 / 632. The arithmetic holds.
- The cases TE-CBB-2 and -8 add are asserts inside existing tests, so the counts stay as stated.
- A different count stops for the advisor (:631).
- Each new test's name is taken from the test runner's own output.
TE condition 5 / TE-CBB-5: ACCEPT. Exactly one new why line in each file, placed (:466-469). The self-test plants the missing line. The placement was checked against the committed P0 files.
TE-CBB-6: ACCEPT (:313-321). Exact values: 2129, 552 and 1530, and B1 2253. The P0 run names (nine) and the P2 run names (five) are asserted in order.

TE-CBB-7: ACCEPT.
- (a) :164-172 and plants CB-P12 and CB-P13: an independent count from for_each_canonical's bytes, down datagrams before the window, stream pieces and acks in it. The bytes were checked in lib.rs.
- (b) :262-263 and plants CB-P14 and CB-P15.
- (c) the shared reader's window, with CB-P8 expecting (A, B) = (1, 1) (:371-372).
- (d) the call site's Err handling is in the rust-reviewer's read (:411-412).
- (e) Summary's L in the bite run equals the clean short run's L (:219-222).
The canonical-bytes assert is kept as a statement that cannot fail; acceptable.
TE-CBB-8: ACCEPT (:268-270). A measured whole hash at a tick with no room record gives B 0, a valid run and no gap, as the frozen row says.
TE-CBB-9: ACCEPT (:622-624). The conjunction is written as the required reading, not as the trigger's condition. My check: on -17's L1 P2 part it covers every other check.
TE-CBB-10: ACCEPT (:365-367). CB-P5 names the assert that fires (the measured sum is above 0) and the value it reports (0).

TE-CBB-11: ACCEPT the deferral (:656-660).
- (i) Only 93509dfd7fd1 is re-judged, since B-3 is confirmed. The test-engineer offered 'or keep B-3', and Mustafa can still name the other folder.
- (ii) The design's old-logs claim is shown by the gaps fixture's first case, and the report must say it was shown by that fixture, not by old logs. That is honest and needs no judge call.

TE-CBB-12: ACCEPT (:580-583). The report's read line names hashed-and-incomplete's move from INVALID to FAIL with its why, the answers for base, lost-group and none-compared, and that no other test's assertion moved.
TE condition 6 (B-1 to B-3 unchanged): ACCEPT. The rulings are recorded at :638-655, and no frozen text changed.
